evidence.label: Guardian aggregate and method
evidence.text: The Guardian reports 387 print stories across UK national newspapers and 99 Sun stories mentioning Flack. Inclusion was her name in headline or body during 14 Aug 2019–14 Feb 2020. Three journalists classified tone; the article says the analysis is not definitive. Most stories were neutral overall; December negative headlines rose to 35% versus 18% positive, while February had equal positive and negative counts.

evidence.label: Charge report, 13 December 2019
evidence.text: ITV reported that Flack was charged with assault by beating on 13 December after an incident the previous day. The allegation was not a conviction.

evidence.label: Flack steps down from Love Island, 17 December 2019
evidence.text: ITV reported that Flack stood down from the upcoming series after the charge. Her statement said reports about her private life did not reflect events as she understood them; she said she would cooperate with authorities and could not comment further during the legal process. ITV accepted her decision.

evidence.label: Laura Whitmore named host, 20 December 2019
evidence.text: ITV announced Laura Whitmore as the replacement host after Flack stepped down; Whitmore described Flack as a friend and said she wished circumstances were better.

evidence.label: Not-guilty plea reported, 24 December 2019
evidence.text: ITV’s 24 December report states Flack pleaded not guilty at Highbury Corner Magistrates’ Court on 23 December. She remained on bail ahead of a trial then scheduled for March. The same report records her statement that scrutiny and speculation were difficult to face alone and that she was taking time away to feel better.

evidence.label: Independent report of Sun story and its removal (secondary)

evidence.label: Removal reported after the window

briefing.title: A fictional desk defence of its sampled coverage

paragraphs.text: We would defend reporting distinct developments in this sample: the charge, Flack’s decision to step down, the replacement host, the plea, and her public response to gossip. These events had public interest because she was a high-profile presenter and the programme was imminent. Our nine retained records are clustered around those changes, not a complete archive.

We would distinguish the allegation from the not-guilty plea and from any later outcome. The charge was not a conviction, and no trial verdict occurred in this window. When Burton’s statements or relationship rumours were reported, we should attribute them and avoid presenting a denial as proof of every underlying claim.

We would say our role is to report verifiable public developments, not turn a private life into ongoing entertainment. Headlines about distress or gossip need particular care. We would ask whether a new item adds information or simply sustains attention after Flack had publicly objected to speculation.

This recovered set is incomplete and event-led. The separately reported print aggregate is not our daily series and cannot establish tone, intent, harm or cause. The Sun Valentine headline is now directly confirmed from its original archived page; the Independent removal report remains a separate secondary source. Readers should distinguish publisher records, later removal coverage and print-aggregate reporting.

briefing.title: A fictional desk defence of its sampled coverage

paragraphs.text: We would defend reporting the charge, Flack’s decision to step down, the replacement host, the court hearing and her Christmas message because each was a dated public development. Our six retained records also include a programme change with direct relevance to viewers and the production.

We would state the procedural facts carefully: the charge was an allegation; Flack pleaded not guilty; the hearing set a future trial. We would include her position and avoid repeating prosecution assertions as established fact. The plea did not resolve the case.

When Flack said scrutiny and speculation were difficult and she was taking a break from social media, we would recognize that as a signal to examine the value of further attention. Public interest in a presenter’s role does not make every detail of her private life newsworthy.

These six retained records are part of an incomplete sample across several outlets. Missing dates do not prove nothing else ran. A separate long-window print aggregate has no itemized daily series here. Counts can prompt questions about repetition and editorial choices, but they do not establish intent or causation.
